case_summary: Recommend how to prevent revoked users from publishing notes through two adapters that share one SQLite owner.
answer: Keep notes.publish as the authority; do not extract a microservice for a small team with no independent deployment or scaling need. Its membership check is separated from the status write, so revocation in after_check can invalidate the earlier read. Replace that check/write gap with one guarded UPDATE: update the note only when its id matches and an EXISTS subquery finds an active membership for the actor and the note's org; derive org from the note, never caller input. Treat one affected row as published and zero as forbidden, then commit as today. The SQLite write statement serializes against a concurrent revocation: whichever write takes effect first determines the result. Both web_publish and cli_publish already call publish, so they retain the same rule without adapter changes. Tradeoff: a compact SQL predicate keeps ownership local but couples the rule to this SQLite query; a service adds deployment and network failure modes without improving this invariant. Verify with a two-connection test: use after_check to revoke membership before the guarded update and assert forbidden/no status change; also race revoke and publish and assert the serial outcome is either revoke-first/forbidden or publish-first/committed. This is a proposal; those checks were not run.
